headword: {年賀状|ねんがじょう}じまい
gloss: ending one's New Year's card custom

definitions.gloss: ending one's New Year's card custom
definitions.explanation: The practice of formally ending the custom of exchanging New Year's cards ({年賀状|ねんがじょう}), usually by sending a final card that announces one will no longer send them. A growing trend, especially among the elderly.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}で{年賀状|ねんがじょう}じまいをする。
examples.english: I'll end my New Year's card custom this year.

examples.japanese: {高齢|こうれい}を{理由|りゆう}に{年賀状|ねんがじょう}じまいをする{人|ひと}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: More people are ending their New Year's card custom citing old age.

examples.japanese: {親|おや}が{年賀状|ねんがじょう}じまいをしたいと{言|い}うので、{文面|ぶんめん}を{一緒|いっしょ}に{考|かんが}えた。
examples.english: My parent said they wanted to stop sending New Year's cards, so we worked out the wording together.

notes:
The suffix 〜じまい (from {仕舞|しま}う, "to finish, to close") means putting an end to a practice. A {年賀状|ねんがじょう}じまい is usually announced on the final card itself.

USAGE:
- A recent social trend tied to {終活|しゅうかつ} (end-of-life preparations) and the spread of digital greetings.

RELATED WORDS:
- {年賀状|ねんがじょう}: New Year's greeting card
- {終活|しゅうかつ}: preparations for the end of one's life
